keyVerseText: And it came to pass, when David was come to Mahanaim, that Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and Machir the son of Ammiel of Lodebar, and Barzillai the Gileadite of Rogelim,
rootMeaning: The name בַּרְזִלַּי (Barzillay) derives from the Hebrew root בַּרְזֶל (barzel), meaning iron, with the suffix indicating 'my iron' or 'man of iron.' This etymology suggests strength, durability, and resilience, qualities associated with iron as a material and tool. The root conveys not only physical hardness but also metaphorical strength or steadfastness, enriching the understanding of the name beyond a mere label to one that implies a robust character.
usageInScripture: Barzillay appears twelve times in Scripture, primarily as a proper name for three distinct individuals, with the majority of references linked to a Gileadite leader who supported King David during Absalom's rebellion. The translations vary slightly, most frequently rendered as 'of Barzillai,' indicating possession or association, but also as 'and Barzillai' or 'Now Barzillai,' reflecting narrative introduction or continuation. This consistency in usage underscores its role as a personal name tied to historical figures noted for loyalty and service.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding Barzillay as 'my iron' highlights the biblical theme of strength and faithfulness in God's servants. The iron metaphor points to a steadfastness that believers are called to emulate, reflecting God's own unchanging nature. The Gileadite Barzillay's support of David in a time of crisis models faithful service and generosity, qualities vital to the community of faith. This name reminds Christians that spiritual resilience and unwavering commitment to God's purposes are marks of true discipleship, grounded in the strength God provides.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Samuel 17:27, Barzillai the Gileadite is mentioned alongside other supporters who came to aid David at Mahanaim. The inclusion of Barzillai here emphasizes his role as a strong and dependable ally during a turbulent period. The name's meaning, 'my iron,' enriches the passage by highlighting the steadfastness and reliability that Barzillai embodied, reinforcing the theme of God's provision through loyal friends in times of trial.
